findings.title: Backup code can bypass password verification
findings.body: Password verification is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is non-empty, while the new branch at line 131 authenticates whenever credentials.backupCode is valid and ignores the TOTP code. An attacker can therefore send a dummy totpCode together with a valid backup code and no correct password and be logged in. A leaked or guessed backup code thus becomes a single-factor credential instead of a replacement second factor; password verification must also run when backupCode is supplied (or whenever the account has a password and this is not the password-less external-TOTP flow).

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing concurrent reuse
findings.body: The code reads the encrypted backup-code list, marks the matched entry null, and writes the whole list back without a transaction, conditional update, or lock. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both read the list before either writes, both find the code, and both authenticate, violating the documented exactly-once property of backup codes. Consumption needs to be made atomic so only one request can claim a code.

findings.title: Backup-code comparison does not normalize case or whitespace
findings.body: Generated codes are lowercase hex, but verification only strips '-' via replaceAll before indexOf; it does not trim whitespace or lowercase the input. A user who types the code in uppercase (as suggested by the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder), or pastes it with surrounding whitespace, is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode even though they entered the correct code. The same un-normalized comparison exists in the disable-2FA endpoint, so normalization should be applied consistently in both places.

findings.title: Users with pre-existing 2FA can never obtain backup codes
findings.body: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature have backupCodes = null. The setup endpoint rejects anyone with twoFactorEnabled already true, and this PR adds no endpoint or settings UI to generate backup codes for an already-enabled account. Such users who click 'Lost access' only get MissingBackupCodes and a message telling them to generate codes in settings, which is impossible without disabling and re-enabling 2FA (and the message does not say that), leaving the recovery path a dead end for all existing 2FA users.

findings.title: resetState leaves backup codes, secret, and download URL in memory
findings.body: resetState only clears the password, error, and step; it never clears backupCodes, dataUri, secret, or backupCodesUrl, and never revokes the Blob object URL. The modal component stays mounted after Close/Cancel, so the plaintext backup codes and a working download URL for them remain live in the page for as long as it is open, contrary to the expectation that closing the backup-code screen discards them. Clear those states and call URL.revokeObjectURL in resetState.

findings.title: No test exercises logging in or disabling with a backup code
findings.body: The added e2e coverage only checks that the download/copy/close buttons work after enabling 2FA; as the TODO on this line admits, nothing tests the actual new authentication paths: login with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, rejection of a wrong code, or rejection when reusing an already-consumed code. These are the security-critical behaviors of the feature (especially single-use invalidation in next-auth-options.ts), and the PR description's own checklist confirms no such tests were added, so a regression in them would ship undetected.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard navigation globally
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide-password button in the shared PasswordField makes the toggle unreachable by keyboard for every form in the app, not just the 2FA modals this PR touches. Keyboard and assistive-technology users can no longer reveal a typed password to check it. This unrelated global accessibility regression should be reverted or scoped to the specific field that motivated it.
